entries.45a9184943952d6e: Transactions in which real estate such as vacant houses bought from sellers is sold to buyers. They are mainly sales of income-producing real estate, detached houses, and condominium units, and revenue is recognized when the property is delivered to the buyer. It is the largest of the categories into which revenue from external customers is divided, for the fiscal year ended December 2025. The securities report states that holding purchased properties as inventory ties up funds and requires registration-related costs and inventory management, so the Company reduces this burden by using contracts for the benefit of a third party (sanni transactions). In a sanni transaction, the seller and the business operator, and the business operator and the buyer, each enter into a sales contract, so registration of ownership in the operator's name is not required and the property is not held as inventory.

entries.a3d9475989873c87: A category of real estate-related transactions that fall under neither real estate sale and purchase transactions nor fee-based takeover transactions. The notes on revenue recognition divide revenue from external customers into three categories: real estate sale and purchase transactions, fee-based takeover transactions and other real estate-related transactions. In the sales results table of the securities report, the MD&A groups fee-based takeover transactions, real estate rental, vacation rental operation and others together as "Other Real Estate-Related." The company started the vacation rental business as a new business in May 2025. This category is a product and service category presented separately in the securities report, not a reportable segment.
entries.a8d4e60ba8e577af: A transaction type in which the company receives money from the seller and takes over the real estate. The securities report states that for properties that are difficult even for the company to purchase because of land prices, building condition and other factors, when there is demand from a buyer, the company may undertake paid consulting on disposing of the property and ultimately purchase it, which in substance amounts to a fee-based takeover. The company is a member of the Real Estate Fee-Based Takeover Council, which aims to improve the soundness of the fee-based real estate takeover industry, and conducts transactions in accordance with its self-regulatory rules. It was included in "Other Real Estate-Related Transactions" in the previous fiscal year, but because its monetary importance has grown, it has been presented separately since the fiscal year ended December 2025.
